headline: New Break seeks $550,000 to fund drilling at its Timmins-area gold project
dek: The flow-through financing would fund exploration spending at the company's Moray project, 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, if it closes as planned.
caption: Flow-through financings like this one are funding further drilling across Ontario's Abitibi gold belt this fall.

sources.title: New Break Announces $550,000 Non-Brokered Private Placement Offering of Flow-Through Shares

unverified_claims: That the offering will close within the next two business days is the company's own statement and has not been independently confirmed.
The 20% carried interest in the Sundog gold project is as disclosed in the company's own description and not independently verified.
brief: New Break Resources Ltd. (CSE: NBRK) said October 30 it intends to complete a non-brokered private placement of up to 2,500,000 flow-through common shares at $0.22 each, for gross proceeds of up to $550,000. The offering is expected to close within two business days, subject to Canadian Securities Exchange approval.

Proceeds will fund Canadian Exploration Expenses at the Moray gold project, 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, the company said. New Break will renounce the expenses to subscribers effective no later than December 31, 2026. The shares carry a four-month-and-one-day statutory hold period.

Qualified finders introducing subscribers may earn a 6% cash fee plus finder warrants equal to 6% of the flow-through shares sold, exercisable at $0.22 for 24 months. New Break also holds a 20% carried interest in Nunavut's Sundog gold project, according to the release.
body: New Break Resources Ltd. (CSE: NBRK) said October 30 that it intends to complete a non-brokered private placement of up to 2,500,000 flow-through common shares at $0.22 per share, for gross proceeds of up to $550,000. The company expects the offering to close within the next two business days, subject to acceptance by the Canadian Securities Exchange and other customary conditions.

The shares qualify as flow-through shares within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada). New Break said the proceeds will be used for Canadian Exploration Expenses, which it will renounce to the purchasers of the shares with an effective date of no later than December 31, 2026, as stated in the release.

The company said the proceeds raised through the offering will go toward ongoing drilling at its Moray gold project, located 49 kilometres southeast of Timmins, Ontario, in the Abitibi greenstone belt. The release gave no drill results or further technical detail on the current program.

Qualified finders who introduce subscribers to the offering may receive a cash fee equal to 6% of the proceeds from those subscribers, plus finder's warrants equal to 6% of the flow-through shares sold to them, exercisable at $0.22 per share for 24 months from closing, according to the release.

All securities issued under the offering, including any finder's warrants, are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, the standard resale restriction under Canadian securities law for this type of exemption.

New Break describes itself as a Canadian mineral exploration company focused primarily on the Moray project, and also holds a 20% carried interest in the Sundog gold project in Nunavut. The release did not disclose the size of New Break's partner's interest in Sundog or any other terms of that arrangement.
